- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 5–10 days.  
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and recent price is trending down; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for next 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if 10–15 days of price is above 30-day MA, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.3 → +0.6), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for next 3–7 days.
